bias.headline: Conditions are modestly bearish (led by Market Breadth) — on thin evidence, so treat the description itself as tentative. This describes the current state, not a prediction.

topBullish.label: Volatility
topBullish.confidenceBasis: 499 prior sessions of this instrument's own ATR history. Confidence is halved deliberately: the volatility-return relationship is a conditional regularity, not a mechanism.
topBullish.explanation: SPY typically moves 0.91% in a day right now — more volatile than 23% of its own past. That is calm, and calm is the condition most steady advances happen in.
topBullish.whyItMatters: Position size and stop distance both scale with volatility, so the same trade is a different risk in a different regime. In equities specifically, expanding volatility tends to accompany falling prices.
topBullish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 23% of them

topBearish.label: Market Breadth
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 95 individual companies, each counted once, against 500 sessions of this panel's own breadth history. A participation count rather than an index proxy — but still a large-cap panel, not a full advance/decline line, so confidence is capped at 75.
topBearish.explanation: 40% of 95 companies are trading above their own 50-session average. That is unusually narrow — higher than only 18% of its own past readings for this group, whose typical session reads 60%.
topBearish.whyItMatters: A rally carried by one or two names is fragile in a way the index level does not show. Broad participation is what separates a durable advance from a narrow one.
topBearish.nextTrigger: stops being bearish if it climbs out of the bottom third of its own past readings — right now it is higher than only 18% of them

topBearish.label: Risk Appetite
topBearish.confidenceBasis: 500 prior sessions of the same credit-minus-duration spread; the current reading is at its 27th percentile.
topBearish.explanation: Over the last 20 trading days riskier corporate bonds are lagging safe government bonds by 0.7% — money is retreating into safety, the classic defensive move.
topBearish.whyItMatters: Credit turns before equity does more often than not. When high yield stops keeping up with Treasuries, the bid for risk is weakening regardless of where the index is trading.

watchNext.label: Trend Strength

conflicts: Net move is positive but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
watchNext.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.15 now

metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 752.18–771.25

metrics.label: Trend Strength
metrics.confidenceBasis: Path efficiency of 0.01 over 60 sessions — the distance actually covered divided by the total ground travelled to cover it (Kaufman's efficiency ratio). Confidence rises with efficiency and reaches 100 at 0.60, a strongly directional path.
metrics.explanation: Over 60 sessions DIA moved +0.4%, and only 1% of its day-to-day movement went toward getting there — the rest was back and forth. That is a round trip rather than a trend, so no direction is claimed from it.

conflicts: Net move is positive but the path is inefficient — the sign is not evidence of a trend.
metrics.nextTrigger: only takes a side once the path gets cleaner — 0.20 of the moves in one direction rather than back and forth, against 0.01 now

metrics.label: Market Structure

metrics.whyItMatters: Structure is the only read that describes the SHAPE of a move rather than its size. Two markets up the same amount are different trades if one is making higher lows and the other keeps undercutting them — and structure is what a stop is placed against.
conflicts: Highs are rising while lows are falling: volatility is expanding without direction.
metrics.nextTrigger: resolves on a close outside 514.04–535.70
